m.combo_pricing.label: Combo/parlay price versus correlated-leg product
m.combo_pricing.measurement: Compute joint probability by simulation with game-level correlation (nfl.corr), compare with executable combo price after fees; verify settlement wording for each leg and void/push handling.
m.combo_pricing.mechanism: A combo's fair price equals the joint probability of legs; naive product of marginals ignores correlation, so a quoted combo price relative to joint model estimate reveals mispricing.
m.combo_pricing.rationale: Combos amplify errors: positively correlated legs (team win and over) are worth more than the product; negatively correlated worth less; also fees and liquidity are larger for combos.

m.stat_correction_risk.label: Official stat correction and settlement-source lag risk
m.stat_correction_risk.measurement: Record the settlement source and observed post-game stat revisions (compare sources at game end and next day); flag ladders where realized value falls within correction tolerance.

nfl.award_milestone_proximity.label: Milestone and record proximity for each candidate
nfl.award_milestone_proximity.measurement: For each candidate and award, list milestone totals from the last 15 years of winners' stat lines (the 20th percentile of winners' totals for each key stat as threshold); compute probability that projected final total exceeds each threshold from the season-to-date accrual model (rate x remaining games with games-played risk); feature = P(exceed) and distance in games. Rolls forward after each week; units: probability.
nfl.award_milestone_proximity.mechanism: Distance of a candidate's projected final total from round-number or record milestones that voters respond to (e.g. 2,000 rushing yards, 5,000 passing yards, 20 sacks, franchise or league records).
nfl.award_milestone_proximity.rationale: Vote probability is not smooth in production: reaching a milestone adds a discrete narrative bump and a record chase draws attention for several weeks, so award probability has a cliff near thresholds.

nfl.award_month_window_games.label: Monthly award window: games, byes and stat accrual inside the calendar window
nfl.award_month_window_games.measurement: For each award month, from the league schedule: games per team in the window (3, 4 or 5); expected stats per game from the candidate's role and an opponent adjustment; window total = sum over games; standard deviation scaled by sqrt(games) with game-level variance from the player's last 20 games. Output probability that the candidate leads the window at his position.
nfl.award_month_window_games.mechanism: Number of games each candidate's team plays in the contract's calendar month and the candidate's stat production within that window.
nfl.award_month_window_games.rationale: Monthly awards are decided on three to five games, so a team on a bye, a rest day or a Thursday game changes the sample; a candidate with five games has more chances than one with three.

nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.label: Backed-up breakaway conversion (P(99-yard TD | snap from own 1))
nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.measurement: Estimate with a hierarchical logistic tail model on all snaps from yardline_100 >= 90 with outcome yards_gained >= 60, then extrapolate to >= 99 with a generalized Pareto tail anchored on the historical 99-yard plays and 80+ yard gains from deep starts; covariates: pass-rush pressure rate, QB deep-ball rate, defence two-high rate, offence tempo; 5-season window, half-life 2 seasons for scheme, shrinkage constant 25 deep-start snaps to the league mean.
nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.mechanism: Conditional probability that a snap taken from the own 1 becomes a full-field touchdown, produced by deep-pass completions behind a single-high or man-coverage defence or by an untouched run.
nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.rationale: The defence is in a compressed field and often in short-yardage or goal-line personnel, which makes a defender-free deep route more plausible on play action, but any penalty (holding, intentional grounding in the end zone) or safety is far likelier than the breakaway. The league sample of true 99-yard plays is a handful in 60 seasons, so the rate must be extrapolated, not counted.

nfl.blowout_continuation_policy.label: Leader's scoring behaviour after the game is decided
nfl.blowout_continuation_policy.measurement: From 2000-2025 pbp, select game states with lead >= 28 in the third or fourth quarter; per head coach, compute points per remaining drive and pass rate versus league expectation for that state; shrink to league mean with 15 drives prior weight; output expected additional points and their distribution per remaining minute. As-of start of week with current coach.
nfl.blowout_continuation_policy.mechanism: Points the leading team keeps adding once the lead exceeds about 35 points, set by the head coach's run-it-up versus kneel tendency, backup quarterback play-calling and whether the trailing team concedes effort.
nfl.blowout_continuation_policy.rationale: A 52-point margin almost never arises from starters alone; it needs fourth-quarter scoring with backups. Coaches differ: some keep throwing and go for it on fourth down, others run the clock. The existing starter-pull input caps starters but says nothing about points scored after the pull.

nfl.broadcast_role_assignment.label: Broadcast and event role assignment model (announced crews, contracts and appearance history)
nfl.broadcast_role_assignment.measurement: P(role) = P(person on the network's announced crew for at least one qualifying event in the window) x P(appears given assigned). Crew assignment is estimated by logistic regression on the person's number of qualifying events in each of the previous 3 seasons (with weights 0.5, 0.3, 0.2), contract end year, the network's announced lead-crew roster (binary), and whether the event is the network's lead broadcast; P(appears | assigned) = 1 minus the withdrawal rate (illness, conflicts) from the past 5 seasons, shrunk with k=10 events toward 0.97. As-of: each network crew press release and contract report, stamped to the hour; before an announcement the prior-season frequency is used.
nfl.broadcast_role_assignment.mechanism: A named person performs a role in a named network's broadcast only if the network assigns them to that event and they appear, which follows announced crew sheets, multi-year talent contracts and prior appearance frequency.
nfl.broadcast_role_assignment.rationale: KXNFLROLE settles on whether a person performs as an on-air analyst in a specific network broadcast in a window; this is a staffing decision with a mostly public paper trail (crew announcements, contract news), not an athletic outcome, and it needs base rates by role type rather than a vote or a season model.
raw_data: network broadcast crew sheets by event and season

nfl.career_record_chase_survival.label: Career record chase: seasons remaining, age decline and retirement hazard
nfl.career_record_chase_survival.measurement: Gap = rung minus career regular-season total as of the last game. Per future season s: P(active in s) from a discrete-time retirement and release hazard by position and age fitted on 1990-2025 players with at least 5 seasons (logit on age, prior-season games and output percentile, k=20 player-seasons shrinkage); output in s = current rate x position aging curve (estimated from 2000-2025 same-position players, ratio by age) x expected games (nfl.games_played_dist). Simulate 20,000 career paths; P(cumulative >= gap before retirement and before the contract expiry). As-of the latest game.
nfl.career_record_chase_survival.mechanism: A career rung set one unit above the all-time record is reached only if the player keeps playing enough seasons at a sufficient rate, so the forecast is a survival-weighted sum over future seasons.
nfl.career_record_chase_survival.rationale: Career contracts in this archetype (passing, receiving, rushing) need the gap to the record, the per-season output path by age and the probability the player retires, is released or is injured out first; a single-season model gives zero information about year three, and the retirement announcement ends the contract.
raw_data: player_stats: player_id, season, position, games, passing_yards, receiving_yards, rushing_yards, rushing_tds

nfl.carry_count_forecast.label: Named-player carry count distribution by script
nfl.carry_count_forecast.measurement: Negative binomial for carries with mean from role share (snap-weighted, half-life 6 games) times team rush attempts (spread-conditioned: mean attempts by closing spread bucket), dispersion by role; shrink share to depth-chart prior with k=3 games; include probability of 0 carries from nfl.injuries_pit; as-of inactive list.
nfl.carry_count_forecast.mechanism: Forecast distribution of the player's number of carries given team spread, game script, role and injury designation.
nfl.carry_count_forecast.rationale: N, the number of draws for the maximum, is overdispersed; a leading team gives the back 25 carries, a trailing team 10; zero for no-play voids.
raw_data: player-game carries, team rush attempts, spread bucket, snaps

nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.label: Clinched-seed rest: expected snap fraction of starters in the final two weeks
nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.measurement: For each team, compute the probability of each clinch state by Week 16 from the standings simulation; from 2015-2025, estimate expected snap fraction in Weeks 17-18 for starters by position as a function of state (clinched top seed, clinched any seed, eliminated), coach-specific rest history (shrink with k=2 occasions), and player age; output expected fraction of normal snaps and its distribution.
nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.mechanism: Probability and magnitude of reduced snaps for starters in Week 17-18 when seeds or division titles are clinched.
nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.rationale: In the final weeks teams with nothing to play for rest key starters, which truncates cumulative totals just when leader races are decided; the effect depends on the coach's history and on the clinch state.

nfl.coach_candidate_hire_model.label: Named-candidate coaching hire probability
nfl.coach_candidate_hire_model.measurement: Expected vacancies V = sum of exit probabilities from nfl.coach_exit_hazard before the date (plus coordinator openings if the contract counts them); candidate share from a conditional logit over 2005-2025 hiring cycles with features: prior head-coach experience and record, years out of coaching, current role, age, number of reported interviews, prior ties to the hiring GM/owner; P(hire) = 1 - exp(-V x share); as-of market time.
nfl.coach_candidate_hire_model.mechanism: Probability that a named candidate is hired as a coach before a date, from the number of expected vacancies, the candidate's profile and interest, and ties to decision-makers with openings.
nfl.coach_candidate_hire_model.rationale: Hire markets depend first on how many jobs open (from exit hazards) and then on candidate share; former head coaches returning, coordinators and media figures have very different conversion rates, and reported interviews are the strongest signal.

nfl.coach_exit_competing_order.label: Competing-risk probability that a named coach is the next head coach out
nfl.coach_exit_competing_order.measurement: Using weekly hazards h_j(t) from nfl.coach_exit_hazard for all 32 coaches from issuance to Feb 15, 2027, compute P(i first) = sum_t h_i(t) prod_j S_j(t-1) prod_{j!=i}(1-h_j(t)) with simultaneous Black Monday exits split by announcement timestamp order (empirical tie-break by time of announcement); residual 'none before deadline' = prod_j S_j(T); recompute weekly as standings update.
nfl.coach_exit_competing_order.mechanism: Probability that coach i's departure occurs before every other permanent head coach's, from all 32 coaches' time-varying exit hazards.
nfl.coach_exit_competing_order.rationale: Next-coach-out pays on order, not occurrence: a coach's chance of being first depends on how hot the other seats are and on when each hazard spikes (in-season vs Black Monday), so per-coach probabilities from nfl.coach_exit_hazard must be combined in a competing-risk calculation.
raw_data: weekly coach hazards for all teams

nfl.coach_exit_hazard.label: Head-coach exit hazard (firing, resignation, pre-announced departure)
nfl.coach_exit_hazard.measurement: Cox or discrete-time logistic hazard with covariates: win% minus preseason expectation (using non-market expectation from ratings), consecutive losses, playoff outcome, years remaining on contract (0-1 vs more), tenure, owner's historical turnover, GM tenure, prior-season record; train on 2000-2025 coach-seasons (about 800); report weekly hazard in-season and post-season; as-of date.
nfl.coach_exit_hazard.mechanism: Hazard of a head coach leaving or announcing departure as a function of record vs expectation, contract status, owner history and calendar.
nfl.coach_exit_hazard.rationale: The contract counts announced exits, so resignations, retirements and mutual parting count; the hazard rises sharply after the season and after specific loss patterns.
raw_data: coach-season table with outcomes and exits

nfl.coach_hot_seat.label: Coaching hot-seat and ownership signals
nfl.coach_hot_seat.measurement: Record vs market-implied win total, consecutive losses, contract years remaining, public ownership statements and insider reports (timestamped); hazard model of in-season/off-season firings by tenure and performance.
nfl.coach_hot_seat.mechanism: Coaching changes are driven by record versus expectation, ownership/GM statements and contract status; these determine the timing and probability of firing/hiring events.
nfl.coach_hot_seat.rationale: Coach-event markets (fired by date, next head coach) hinge on organizational behavior; relevant data are records vs preseason expectation, statements, and media reporting rather than game statistics.

nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.label: Coach surprise: wins above own pre-season expectation
nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.measurement: Pre-season expected wins = sum over remaining games of own win probability from team rating (roster continuity regression of last-year EPA, QB change, strength of schedule); surprise = (projected final wins from standings simulation) - pre-season expected wins; add division title and playoff seed bonuses based on historical winners; units: wins above expectation.
nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.mechanism: Team win total minus the expected wins from a pre-season rating built without betting-market inputs (own roster and last-year efficiency prior).
nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior.rationale: Coach of the Year is a vote for surprise rather than quality, so the relevant measure is outcome minus prior expectation; using a sportsbook win total would import a market price as an input, so the prior must be from the model's own rating.

nfl.combine_attempt_noise_best_of_k.label: Within-prospect attempt noise and best-of-attempts uplift
nfl.combine_attempt_noise_best_of_k.measurement: From seasons where both 40 attempts and all jump attempts are published, estimate within-prospect sd by drill and position via random-effects model; where only best marks exist, infer sd from the gap between Combine and pro-day results for prospects who ran both (sd_attempt = sd_gap / sqrt(2) after removing a mean surface effect). Output sd and expected best-of-k uplift; units seconds and inches.
nfl.combine_attempt_noise_best_of_k.mechanism: The recorded value is the best of a prospect's attempts, so the expected recorded extreme exceeds his mean by an amount that rises with attempt variance and attempt count.
nfl.combine_attempt_noise_best_of_k.rationale: Attempt-to-attempt 40 variation (start reaction, stumbles, hamstring tightness) is roughly a few hundredths (unsourced estimate until fitted); best-of-two shifts the expected best by roughly 0.56 sd. For a record-break threshold or a close argmax, this variance matters as much as the mean.
raw_data: combine attempt-level forty_1, forty_2 when published

nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history.label: Yearly Combine best marks by drill and record tail
nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history.measurement: Collect yearly best and top-5 marks for the 40 (history window start provisional, see unresolved u5: electronic timing may predate 2006 and later system changes are unidentified) and broad jump, 2006-2025; fit a GEV distribution with location linear in season and in log(number of participants in speed positions); bootstrap the shape parameter; output P(max broad >= 148) and the distribution of the winning 40 time. As-of before testing.
nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history.mechanism: Distribution of the yearly fastest 40 and longest broad jump across classes, used to calibrate the extreme-value tail and the chance of breaking the record.
nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history.rationale: The 148-inch strike exceeds the 147-inch record, so the per-class probability is a record-exceedance tail that cannot be read from typical yearly bests; the era trend (training specialisation) and the number of participants shift the location.

nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard.label: Combine drill opt-in probability per invitee and drill
nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard.measurement: Logistic model of P(performed drill | invited) by drill, fit on 2010-2025 Combine data (missing value with player present = skip): covariates projected draft round from consensus board at invite date, injury reported in prior 60 days (yes/no), position, prior 40 tier; shrink team-agency effects with 20 prospects of prior weight. Update to 0 or 1 on credible reports in the final week; as-of each report timestamp.
nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard.mechanism: Each invitee independently decides whether to perform each drill in Indianapolis; skipping is driven by injury, draft-stock risk and preference for a pro-day surface.
nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard.rationale: Opt-out is non-random: projected top picks and injured players skip more, and the fastest players sometimes run anyway to set records. Because the 40 contract is an argmax, a single opt-out of the best prior moves several percent of probability to each remaining contender.
raw_data: combine.forty, broad_jump null flags by player

nfl.combine_invite_pool_position_mix.label: Combine invite pool size and position mix (aggregate of per-prospect priors, used as a covariate)
nfl.combine_invite_pool_position_mix.measurement: From the official invite list as of release date: counts by listed position, and for each drill the number of invitees whose nfl.prospect_pre_combine_athletic_prior is faster than 4.40 s (40) or longer than 130 inches (broad), regardless of position. Derived aggregate of the per-prospect prior: in the per-prospect simulation it adds no information, and it is used only as the log(participants) covariate of the historical GEV fit in nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history. Compare to 2006-2025 classes as z-scores. As-of: invite release, refreshed with late additions.
nfl.combine_invite_pool_position_mix.mechanism: The invite list fixes the field over which the fastest 40 and longest jump are taken. Candidates for the extreme come from any position with a fast prior (WR, CB, S, RB, and also edge, LB, TE for the jump), so the pool is filtered by prior, not by listed position.
nfl.combine_invite_pool_position_mix.rationale: Yearly extremes vary with class composition: a class heavy in undersized receivers and corners produces more sub-4.35 runs and 11-foot jumps. Non-invited small-school prospects cannot settle the contract even if faster, so the invite list, not the draft class, defines the field.

nfl.combine_timing_protocol_and_venue.label: Combine timing protocol, track surface and unofficial-to-official revision
nfl.combine_timing_protocol_and_venue.measurement: For each Combine since 2015: document timing system and start method from league releases; compute mean and sd of (official minus first-displayed unofficial) 40 times from captured broadcast or tracker snapshots; flag years with a declared timing or surface change as regime breaks; output revision distribution in seconds and a regime indicator.
nfl.combine_timing_protocol_and_venue.mechanism: How the recorded number is produced: electronic start and finish timing, indoor track surface, attempt rules, and the revision of broadcast unofficial times to official times.
nfl.combine_timing_protocol_and_venue.rationale: Unofficial broadcast times and official results can differ by a few hundredths, and timing-system changes across years shift the whole distribution; both matter for an argmax among sprinters separated by 0.01-0.03 s and for comparing a record across eras.

nfl.common_availability_shock.label: Shared availability shock across legs (QB, WR1, OL, kicker)
nfl.common_availability_shock.measurement: Define lineup states (QB1/QB2, WR1 in/out, starting kicker, RT in/out) with probabilities from injury designation base rates (shrink to position-level, k=10 games); condition each leg on state using prior-season splits with k=3 games shrinkage; joint = sum over states of P(state) x product of conditional legs adjusted by in-state dependence. As-of per injury report vintage.
nfl.common_availability_shock.mechanism: One lineup event (QB scratch, kicker injury, star WR late scratch) moves several legs of the same combo simultaneously.
nfl.common_availability_shock.rationale: Legs priced early assume a baseline lineup; a late change lowers the QB yards leg, total and favourite-cover jointly, so the joint probability is a mixture over lineup states rather than a product.

nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.label: Pairwise covariance of remaining output among contenders
nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.measurement: From 2012-2025 player-seasons, estimate residual correlation between remaining-season output of pairs (same team same stat; QB-WR pairs; RB-RB) after removing season-level means, using the last 8 weeks as the test window; shrink pairwise correlation to the category average with k=30 pairs; use in a multivariate normal or copula simulation of the contender field.
nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.mechanism: Covariance of remaining-season output between contenders sharing a team, position room or quarterback.
nfl.contender_pairwise_covariance.rationale: Leader probability involves the probability that one exceeds the other, so independence overstates the probability of both being high; teammates' rushing is negatively linked, and passing and receiving of a QB and his top receiver positively.

nfl.contract_value_comps.label: Positional contract value comps scaled by cap growth
nfl.contract_value_comps.measurement: For position p, take contracts signed in the last 24 months, express APY as % of the cap in the signing year; fit a quantile regression of APY%cap on player value (prior 2-season EPA or PFF-free equivalent production metrics), age and contract-year status; predicted APY = quantiles x projected cap of the signing year; report the distribution of total value = APY x expected years; as-of market time.
nfl.contract_value_comps.mechanism: Expected new-contract value (APY and total) for a player from recent comparable contracts at the position, scaled to the projected salary cap.
nfl.contract_value_comps.rationale: Next-contract-size markets depend on how the market for the position has moved; the most recent top contract at the position resets the scale and cap growth shifts all values, while age and injury discount it.
raw_data: contracts: player, position, sign date, years, total, APY, guarantees

nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.label: Count-statistic dispersion by stat and score-state split
nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.measurement: From 2012-2025 team-games fit, per stat, a negative binomial with mean = opportunities x rate and dispersion k by stat and by score-state bucket (lead>=14, within 7, trail>=14); shrink k toward the league-stat value with a gamma prior (equivalent to 200 team-games); output PMF for each stat given expected mean and state mixture over the pre-game margin distribution.
nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.mechanism: Negative-binomial dispersion parameters and mean multipliers for field goals, sacks, interceptions, rushing attempts and yards by score state and game total.
nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.rationale: Thresholds like 4+ field goals or 6+ sacks are tail masses; a Poisson assumption understates them, and dispersion changes with whether the game is a blowout or a close contest.
raw_data: team-game counts: field goals made, sacks, interceptions, rush attempts, total yards, with score differential history

nfl.cross_game_leg_dependence.label: Residual dependence between win legs of different games on one slate
nfl.cross_game_leg_dependence.measurement: For every pair of games in the same week 2012-2025 (regular season and playoffs separately), compute residuals e_g = 1{home win} - p_model_g using point-in-time model win probabilities from nfl.model_margin_lattice (OT included, ties scored 0.5); estimate the pooled pairwise correlation of e_g within week, and conditional on both games outdoor with forecast wind >15 mph and on both favourites p>0.7; shrink toward 0 with a prior of n0=2000 pairs; output rho and its standard error per regime, as-of previous season.
nfl.cross_game_leg_dependence.mechanism: Correlation between the outcomes of different games after conditioning on each game's model win probability, arising from shared model error, shared weather fronts and league-wide officiating trends.
nfl.cross_game_leg_dependence.rationale: Multi-game moneyline parlays are priced as a product of legs; if residual outcome correlation is non-zero (e.g. the model systematically overrates favourites in one week or one weather regime), the product misprices the parlay. Expected to be near zero, but must be measured rather than assumed because errors compound across 3 legs.
raw_data: games: game_id, season, week, game_type, home_team, away_team, home_score, away_score, roof, wind, temp

nfl.cross_league_futures_leg.label: Cross-league futures leg marginal and dependence
nfl.cross_league_futures_leg.measurement: P(combo) = P_NFL(team wins Super Bowl) x P_other(team wins title) x (1 + rho_adj), with P_NFL from nfl.standings_sim playoff simulation (20,000 seasons) and P_other the other sport's catalog championship model output taken as-of the same timestamp; rho_adj set to 0 unless a shared-owner or shared-market effect is shown (test: correlation of preseason title probabilities across leagues by metro 2000-2025, expected near 0). Record both legs' as-of times and the date each leg can first resolve NO.
nfl.cross_league_futures_leg.mechanism: A cross-league championship combo is the product of an NFL title probability and another league's title probability, adjusted for any shared dependence (near zero) and for the different resolution dates.
nfl.cross_league_futures_leg.rationale: The NFL leg comes from the season simulation, but the other leg (NBA champion) is outside every NFL input; without an explicit import of that sport's model output, with its own as-of time, the combo cannot be priced. Dependence between the legs is close to independence but resolution timing makes early NO paths matter for mark-to-market.
raw_data: NFL season simulation output by team and date
other-league championship probability by team and date
playoff elimination dates for both leagues

nfl.cross_period_score_dependence.label: Cross-quarter dependence of team scoring
nfl.cross_period_score_dependence.measurement: Compute tetrachoric correlations of team-scored-in-quarter indicators across quarter pairs from 2015+ team-games, split by team offensive EPA tercile; compare to the independence benchmark; shrink pairwise estimates toward the pooled with k=300 games; as-of season-to-date.
nfl.cross_period_score_dependence.mechanism: The correlation between a team scoring in quarter j and in quarter k, accounting for pace, quality and clock burn.
nfl.cross_period_score_dependence.rationale: Every-quarter BTTS and 1H/2H combos require the joint of period events, which differs from the product of marginals.

nfl.deep_tail_margin_model.label: Blowout tail model for margins above 21 points
nfl.deep_tail_margin_model.measurement: Fit generalized Pareto (threshold 21) to |margin| for 2000+ games with covariates: |model expected margin| bucket from nfl.model_team_points_mean, backup QB, model total; estimate shape xi with bootstrap CI; expected number of games above k in a season = sum over games of P(|M|>k); for season max compute 1 - prod(1 - p_g); as-of start of week.
nfl.deep_tail_margin_model.mechanism: Extreme-margin probability as a function of mismatch, QB state, turnover snowballing and weather.
nfl.deep_tail_margin_model.rationale: Deep rungs (20+) and season-maximum blowout contracts are priced on the tail and a normal fit materially understates them; the distribution of margins above 28 across 2000+ is thick.
raw_data: final scores 2000-2025, model mean margin and total regime (market-free)

nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.label: Defence sack-count decomposition: opponent dropbacks, pressure rate, conversion
nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.measurement: Expected opponent dropbacks from nfl.pace and nfl.script; team pressure rate over last 12 games (half-life 6, shrink k=120 dropbacks); conversion = sacks / pressures with opposing quarterback's career-regressed rate (shrink k=100 pressures) and pass-rusher availability adjustment; E[sacks] = dropbacks x pressure rate x conversion; add overdispersion from the count model. Needs pressure data or a sack-plus-hit proxy.
nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.mechanism: Expected sacks by this defence equal opponent expected dropbacks times pressure rate times pressure-to-sack conversion, with opposing quarterback's sack avoidance and the offence's pass protection.
nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition.rationale: The 6+ sacks contract is a tail of a thin count; the mean depends on three multiplicative factors with different regression speeds, and the conversion factor is quarterback specific.
raw_data: pbp: sack, qb_hit, qb_dropback, passer, defteam

nfl.defense_target_funnel_share.label: Defensive target funnel: share of opponent targets allowed by alignment and position
nfl.defense_target_funnel_share.measurement: For each defence: over the last 12 games (half-life 6 games) compute target shares by alignment, adjusted for opponent offence's usual share using a ridge model (alpha tuned by cross-season validation); shrink toward league with k=100 targets. Output: log ratio of expected share vs the receiver's usual share. Needs alignment tags from charting data.
nfl.defense_target_funnel_share.mechanism: Fraction of opposing pass targets a defence allows to WRs (slot and outside), TEs and RBs, relative to league and adjusted for the offences it faced.
nfl.defense_target_funnel_share.rationale: Defence-versus-position yield tells how efficient receivers are against a defence but not how many targets it sends to each group, which sets a receiver's share before efficiency matters.
raw_data: target by position/alignment, defteam, play type

nfl.depth_chart_publication_lag.label: Depth-chart publication mechanics and lag by team
nfl.depth_chart_publication_lag.measurement: Per team-week from archive of depth charts (team websites and nflverse depth_charts), record publication weekday, whether an 'or' slot is used, change relative to prior week; compute P(chart lists a different QB1 than the actual week's starter); as-of week.
nfl.depth_chart_publication_lag.mechanism: How and when each team publishes its official depth chart and how 'starter' is encoded.
nfl.depth_chart_publication_lag.rationale: First-start contracts settle on the published chart; teams differ on publication day and encoding (or-designations), so the label can differ from who actually starts.

nfl.designation_to_play_calibration.label: Practice-sequence and designation to play-probability calibration
nfl.designation_to_play_calibration.measurement: Hierarchical logistic regression of played (>=1 snap) on practice-sequence pattern (e.g., DNP-LP-FP), designation, position group, days of rest, and team random effect with shrinkage prior (tau fitted); training 2012-2025 injury reports with vintages; as-of each report time; output P(play) with credible interval.
nfl.designation_to_play_calibration.mechanism: Calibrated P(plays | Wednesday, Thursday, Friday practice status, designation, position, team, week).
nfl.designation_to_play_calibration.rationale: The mapping is team-specific: some teams use Questionable for near-certain players, others reserve it for coin flips; position matters because linemen and skill players differ.

nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.label: First-overall-pick race: bottom of standings, strength-of-schedule tiebreak and pick ownership
nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.measurement: Simulate final records, take the minimum-wins team with the league's draft-order tiebreak (lower strength of schedule gets the higher pick, as an assumption flagged SOURCE_UNVERIFIED), then map the draft slot owner via a table of traded picks; add a small tanking adjustment (reduced win probability for teams eliminated by Week 12, estimated from history).
nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.mechanism: Distribution of the team that ultimately makes the first pick, from the worst-record contest with its tiebreak and from ownership of traded picks.
nfl.draft_first_pick_loser_race.rationale: The first-pick contract depends on who has the worst record, the tiebreak for ties (strength of schedule rather than team strength) and whether the pick has been traded, so it is an extreme-value problem of losing, not winning.

nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.label: Draft order rules engine (season result to overall slot)
nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.measurement: Implement league draft-order rules: non-playoff teams ascending by win percentage, ties broken by strength of schedule then divisional and conference tiebreakers; picks 19-24 wild card losers, 25-28 divisional losers, 29-30 conference-final losers, 31 Super Bowl loser, 32 champion; apply the league's list of forfeited picks. Run on simulated seasons from the season simulation to give the slot distribution per team; as-of = latest game result and the official pick-transaction list.
nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.mechanism: Deterministic mapping from final standings, playoff results and tiebreakers to round-one overall slots 1-32 (champion 32, Super Bowl loser 31), repeated in each round; compensatory picks and later rounds are handled by nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks.
nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.rationale: Slot ownership before the draft is not a model output but a rules calculation on results that are still uncertain in November: non-playoff teams are ordered by record then strength of schedule, playoff teams by round exited, so the 32nd pick equals the Super Bowl winner. Forfeitures can shorten a round and shift overall numbering.

nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.label: Draft pick ownership and trade graph (who holds each slot, trade-up hazard)
nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.measurement: Maintain a table of pick-by-pick ownership for all seven rounds with transaction timestamps; estimate P(slot k traded before selection) with a logistic on slot, consensus gap between the top prospects, holder's quarterback need and asset stock, fitted on the last 15 drafts with shrinkage toward the empirical draft-wide trade rate for the same slot band (estimated, no fixed prior asserted); as-of = the latest official trade list.
nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.mechanism: Current owner of each first-round pick, the set of future-pick bundles, and the chance a slot changes hands before or on draft night.
nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.rationale: Contracts settle on the team that ultimately makes the pick and on pick-order outcomes, so ownership at the moment of selection is the relevant variable. Trade-ups for a quarterback, by a team that holds a later pick, are the main way that consensus order is broken, and there is a documented pre-draft window when picks are exchanged.

nfl.draft_position_label_governance.label: Draft position label governance (official position classification)
nfl.draft_position_label_governance.measurement: Build a label table from the league's draft tracker position at the time of selection and compare with the college and consensus-board labels for the last 10 classes; compute the disagreement rate by position pair (EDGE versus DL versus LB, S versus CB, OT versus OG) and carry it as probability mass into Nth-at-position markets; as-of = each pick announcement.
nfl.draft_position_label_governance.mechanism: Mapping from a prospect to the position label that settles contracts (QB, RB, WR, TE, OL, DL, EDGE, LB, DB), including how the governing league and source agencies label hybrid players.
nfl.draft_position_label_governance.rationale: Position-drafted and Nth-at-position contracts depend on labels, and the rules text states that if positions differ across source agencies the Governing League's position is used. Edge rushers, hybrid linebackers and safeties-cornerbacks and tackle-guard swaps are exactly where labels diverge.

nfl.draft_qb_class_model.label: Draft positional-selection model (QB class order, draft order, team need and trade-up)
nfl.draft_qb_class_model.measurement: Plackett-Luce ordering model over the QBs in the class: utility_j = -beta*ln(consensus_rank_j) + gamma*need(team on the clock) with consensus_rank an average of at least 5 public big boards (time-stamped; weights proportional to each board's historical rank-correlation with actual draft order), beta and gamma fit by maximum likelihood on 2010-2025 drafts (about 180 QBs), team need = 1 if the current starter contract expires within one year or the starter's EPA per play is below the league 25th percentile; draft order from the final standings and traded picks. Simulate 20,000 drafts including a trade-up probability for QB-needy teams outside the top 5 (estimated from the 2010-2025 share of QBs taken before their consensus slot, shrunk with k=5). Report P(QB j is the k-th QB selected) and P(QB j drafted in the top n). As-of: refreshed after the combine, pro days, and each time a credible insider reports intentions; final run at draft start. Betting or market odds are excluded and used as benchmarks only.
nfl.draft_qb_class_model.mechanism: The k-th quarterback drafted is determined by the ranked order in which teams on the clock select QBs, which depends on consensus prospect rank, the order of picks of QB-needy teams, and trades that move teams up.
nfl.draft_qb_class_model.rationale: Draft contracts such as 'player X is the 3rd quarterback drafted' are order statistics over a small class (about 8 to 14 QBs drafted per year), where a single early-round team's need and a trade-up change the rank of all later QBs. The generic consensus-board input gives one prospect's rank but not the joint ordering that the count-based contract settles on.

team QB contract and starter performance

nfl.drive_clock_allocation.label: Drive-start allocation across periods (clock-resolved)
nfl.drive_clock_allocation.measurement: From pbp: for each team-game, count drives starting in Q1..Q4 and seconds per drive by period; use 20-game recency weights (half-life 8) and opponent-adjust by regressing on opponent pace; combine with kickoff order to produce expected starts for each quarter and the probability of a second drive in Q1. Shrink to league mean with k=10 games.
nfl.drive_clock_allocation.mechanism: The number of drives that begin in each quarter, and where the quarter ends relative to drive boundaries, for both teams.
nfl.drive_clock_allocation.rationale: Quarter totals depend on counts of starts and finishes in a 15-minute window; a game-level drives estimate ignores kickoff order, tempo by period, and clock burn.
raw_data: pbp: drive, qtr, drive_start_game_seconds_remaining, drive_end, drive_plays, posteam

nfl.drive_duration_by_outcome.label: Drive duration distribution by outcome and team style
nfl.drive_duration_by_outcome.measurement: From pbp: drive_time_of_possession by outcome for each team over the last 20 games (half-life 10); opponent adjustment by regression on the opponent's allowed durations; fit a lognormal for each outcome class with team-level scale shrunk to league with k=15 drives; as-of previous game; clock-converted to elapsed game clock including quarter-end stops.
nfl.drive_duration_by_outcome.mechanism: Seconds of game clock consumed by TD drives, FG drives, punts and turnovers for each team and opponent.
nfl.drive_duration_by_outcome.rationale: The time of the first TD (and bucket probabilities) is a convolution of these durations, so mean pace is insufficient; the right tail matters for late buckets.

free_sources: nflverse pbp (drive-level via fixed_drive and drive result)
nfl.drive_outcome_by_index.label: Per-drive outcome probabilities by drive index and starting field position
nfl.drive_outcome_by_index.measurement: Fit multinomial logit (TD, FG, punt, turnover, other) on the first four team drives of each game 2015+ with covariates: team offence random effect, opponent defence random effect, starting yardline_100; recency half-life 15 games; shrink team early-drive effect toward its all-drive effect with k=25 early drives; as-of previous game.
nfl.drive_outcome_by_index.mechanism: Multinomial outcome of drive 1, 2 and 3 for each team, conditional on starting yard line and opponent.
nfl.drive_outcome_by_index.rationale: The first drive is scripted and starts from a kickoff; season-average drive efficiency misses the hazard that matters for first-score contracts.
raw_data: pbp: fixed_drive, fixed_drive_result, posteam, yardline_100 at drive start, game_seconds_remaining

nfl.drive_result_lattice.label: Drive-result lattice: touchdown, field goal, turnover, punt probabilities by start position
nfl.drive_result_lattice.measurement: From drive-level play-by-play 2016-2025 estimate multinomial logit of drive result on start yard line, offence rating, defence rating, down-and-distance style, with team-level random effects (shrink team deviations with k=10 drives); output P(TD), P(FG), P(none) for each of 11 drives by start-position distribution and compute the discrete points distribution by convolution including 2-point and XP outcomes.
nfl.drive_result_lattice.mechanism: Per-drive probabilities of touchdown, field goal and no score for this offence against this defence conditioned on starting field position and game state.
nfl.drive_result_lattice.rationale: Team points are the convolution of drive outcomes, not a smooth function of EPA per play: two offences with equal EPA can have different touchdown-to-field-goal mixes, and the mixture decides the cluster of the score.
raw_data: drive: start_yard_line, result, points, posteam, defteam, plays, time

nfl.dst_td_hazard.label: Defensive and special-teams TD hazard per team-game
nfl.dst_td_hazard.measurement: Per team-game rate = 0.5*(own takeaway-return TD rate regressed to league mean with k=40 team games + opponent giveaway rate) + returner threat (kick and punt return TD per return, k=60 returns) + opponent special teams allowed rate. Poisson mean; as-of previous game.
nfl.dst_td_hazard.mechanism: Pick-sixes, fumble returns, punt and kick return TDs happen at low frequency and are partly attributable to scheme and returner skill but largely random.
nfl.dst_td_hazard.rationale: These events end the 'first TD' contest for every offensive player and count in the team first-TD and D/ST TD markets; they are about 1 in 8-10 team games.
raw_data: pbp: interception_return_td flags, fumble_recovery_return_td, kickoff/punt returner id

nfl.early_nonoffensive_score_hazard.label: Early-game non-offensive scoring hazard (pick-six, return TD, safety)
nfl.early_nonoffensive_score_hazard.measurement: Hazard per team-game of non-offensive TD (own takeaway returns + returner threat + opponent giveaways) and safety, estimated over 3 seasons with k=40 team-games shrinkage; allocate within the first 15 game minutes using the empirical share of such events by quarter (about one quarter of events); as-of previous game.
nfl.early_nonoffensive_score_hazard.mechanism: Probability of a defensive, return or safety score in the first half of the opening quarter or before the first offensive TD.
nfl.early_nonoffensive_score_hazard.rationale: Such scores pre-empt the race and occur on a different hazard from offensive drives; ignoring them biases first-team probabilities toward the stronger offence.
raw_data: pbp: interception, fumble_lost, return TDs, safety

nfl.endzone_exposure_plays.label: End-zone exposure plays per team-game
nfl.endzone_exposure_plays.measurement: From pbp: per team-game count of offensive plays with yardline_100>=95 plus punts with yardline_100>=90, with a per-play safety probability by play type (sack, run, pass, punt) from 2010+ league data, team factor shrunk with k=30 exposed plays; recency half-life 20 games; expected safeties = sum count x probability; as-of previous game.
nfl.endzone_exposure_plays.mechanism: Count of offensive plays run with the ball inside the team's own 5-yard line and punts from within the own end zone or 5, which are the sites of most safeties.
nfl.endzone_exposure_plays.rationale: Safeties scale with exposure; a team that starts drives deep and has a poor punt unit has several times more exposed plays than another.
raw_data: pbp: yardline_100, play_type, sack, safety, punt_blocked, punt_in_endzone

nfl.event_calendar_hazard.label: Calendar-structured hazard curve by event type
nfl.event_calendar_hazard.measurement: From the transaction wire and coach history 2000-2025, count events per calendar week by type; estimate piecewise-constant weekly hazard with Gamma-Poisson shrinkage (prior shape 2, rate 4 pseudo-team-years); condition on state (team win % bin, contract year remaining); compute P(event in [now, deadline]) = 1 - exp(-sum of hazard x exposure); as-of date.
nfl.event_calendar_hazard.mechanism: Time-varying hazard of each event type (coach exit, retirement, signing, trade, cut) across the league calendar.
nfl.event_calendar_hazard.rationale: Contracts with fixed dates (before Mar 1, 2027) integrate the hazard over uneven time; ignoring the spikes (Black Monday, cut-down, deadline) misallocates probability across the window.

nfl.executive_move_attribution.label: Executive of the Year attribution: win surprise explained by front-office moves
nfl.executive_move_attribution.measurement: For each team-season: win surprise = actual wins minus own pre-season expected wins (from nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior's prior); acquisition share = snap-weighted approximate value (PFR AV) of players new to the roster this season (trades, free agents, rookies) divided by total team AV; new-coach flag. Score = win surprise x (0.5 + acquisition share) + 1.0 x new-coach flag; softmax over teams with temperature fitted to PFWA winners 2000-2025, candidate shrinkage k=5 seasons. As-of each week; final as-of end of regular season.
nfl.executive_move_attribution.mechanism: Scores each team's general manager by the team's wins above its own pre-season expectation, weighted by the share of that surprise attributable to new acquisitions, the draft class and a new head coach.
nfl.executive_move_attribution.rationale: The PFWA executive vote rewards a visible turnaround that writers credit to roster building; a team that over-performs on luck or an incumbent star does not earn the same credit, so win surprise alone over-predicts and the attribution share is the subtle part.
raw_data: player-season AV and acquisition type (trade, FA, draft)
PFWA Executive of the Year winners by year

nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.label: Play-level expected touchdowns (xTD) from opportunity location
nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.measurement: Fit a logistic model on 2016-2025 plays: P(TD | yardline_100, down, ydstogo, play type, air yards, role) for carries and targets, then player xTD per game = sum of play probabilities over the last 12 games with half-life 6, shrunk toward position-role mean with k=4 games; forecast = xTD rate x projected opportunities; compare actual TD minus xTD for regression diagnostics.
nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.mechanism: Sum over a player's carries and targets of the probability that the play scores a touchdown given its yard line, distance to go and air yards.
nfl.expected_touchdowns_by_play_location.rationale: Touchdowns are the largest fantasy variance source and regress strongly; share of red-zone usage alone is a coarse measure, while a play-level expected touchdown count is a direct estimate of true touchdown rate.
raw_data: pbp: yardline_100, down, ydstogo, rusher_id, receiver_id, air_yards, touchdown flag

nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.label: Component and teammate-stack covariance of fantasy points
nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.measurement: From 2012-2025 player-game data compute the correlation between components within a player and between pairs of teammates, by position pair, after removing team-week means; shrink pairwise correlations to position-pair averages with k=80 games; use a Gaussian or t-copula for joint simulation. Output a correlation matrix per game by team and position and variance multipliers for total scores.
nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.mechanism: Correlation matrix of a player's scoring components (receptions, yards, touchdowns) and between teammates' scores (quarterback-receiver, same-backfield).
nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covarian.rationale: Variance of the fantasy total is mostly covariance, and head-to-head, top-N and ladder markets depend on it; a quarterback touchdown pass produces four points for him and six for his receiver, which the sum-of-marginals logic ignores.
raw_data: player-game components: pass yards, pass TD, rush yards, rush TD, receptions, receiving yards, receiving TD, INT, fumbles lost

nfl.fourth_and_goal_policy.label: 4th-and-goal and goal-to-go go-for-it policy
nfl.fourth_and_goal_policy.measurement: Go-for-it rate on 4th-and-goal with ydstogo <= 3 over the last 2 seasons, opponent and win-probability adjusted: logistic regression on wp, ydstogo, score_differential, time; coach-level random effect with k=12 attempts shrinkage; as-of last game of the prior week; flagged on coach change.
nfl.fourth_and_goal_policy.mechanism: On 4th-and-goal from inside the 2-3 yards, coaches either kick a FG or go for the TD, changing the number of TDs and the target and carry mix on those snaps.
nfl.fourth_and_goal_policy.rationale: TD pool is what matters, not points; two teams with equal implied totals can differ by half a TD per game because of this choice. It also drives who receives the final-yard touches.
raw_data: pbp: down, ydstogo, yardline_100, wp, go-for-it flag via play_type

nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.label: Fourth-down go-for-it versus field-goal decision rate and two-point policy
nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.measurement: For each head coach over 3 seasons: P(go | yard line bin, distance bin, score and time bin), shrink to model-based optimum with k=15 decisions; two-point attempts per touchdown shrunk with k=10; expected points per stalled drive = P(go) x [conv x 7 + (1-conv) x 0] + (1-P(go)) x P(make FG | distance) x 3; output delta in expected points per game and variance. As-of last completed game.
nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.mechanism: Coach-specific probability of going for it on fourth down by field position and distance, and of attempting a two-point conversion.
nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.rationale: The decision converts a stalled drive into 3 points, 0 points or 7 points; aggressive coaches raise the variance and shift the mean of team totals, and two-point attempts change points per touchdown.
raw_data: pbp: down, ydstogo, yardline_100, play_type, field_goal_result, two_point_attempt

nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks.label: Full seven-round draft order with compensatory picks (who holds each of about 257 selections)
nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks.measurement: Build rounds 1-7 from the rules engine order; forecast compensatory picks per team from net free-agent losses and the public compensatory formula projections until the official March release, then use the official list; apply forfeits and traded-pick ownership; output, per slot, the holding team distribution and the overall pick number of round boundaries (end of round 2, end of round 3) and of the final selection.
nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks.mechanism: Round-by-round order repeats the round-one order, with compensatory selections (awarded in March under the free-agency formula and special minority-hiring picks) appended at the ends of rounds 3-7 and forfeitures removed; the last of these is the final selection.
nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks.rationale: The last-pick, school-count, rounds 1-3 and pick-64 series settle beyond round one, where ownership depends on compensatory awards and late trades. Before March the number and placement of compensatory picks are uncertain, so the identity and team of the last pick is a distribution.

free-agent signings and losses with contract values

nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.label: Full-strength playoff rating versus season-average rating
nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.measurement: Compute opponent-adjusted efficiency (EPA/play margin) over games where the current starting QB and at least 80 percent of current starters (by snap weight) played, excluding Week 18 rested-starter games and fourth-quarter garbage time (win probability >95 percent); shrink to the season average with k=5 games; output rating in points of margin and the difference from season average as an adjustment for playoff-round probabilities.
nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.mechanism: Team rating computed on games with the current starting lineup (healthy QB, lines, defence) excluding games with rested starters or garbage time.
nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.rationale: Regular-season averages include injuries that have healed and rested-starter games in Weeks 17-18, which bias the rating used for playoffs and title futures.

nfl.game_fantasy_max_field_sim.label: Single-game fantasy maximum: joint simulation of both rosters under ESPN PPR scoring
nfl.game_fantasy_max_field_sim.measurement: For each game: draw team drives and touchdowns from the team scoring model, attribute each touchdown to passer/receiver or rusher by player share (targets, carries, red-zone share over last 8 games, half-life 4), draw yards and receptions conditional on attributed plays from player component models (nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covariance), score each player with ESPN default PPR weights (1 per reception, 0.1 per rushing/receiving yard, 0.04 per passing yard, 4 per passing TD, 6 per rush/receiving TD, -2 per interception and lost fumble under ESPN defaults, to be verified); 20,000 simulations; P(max) per player with 1/N for exact ties. As-of kickoff with final inactives.
nfl.game_fantasy_max_field_sim.mechanism: Simulates every relevant player's ESPN-PPR fantasy score in one game jointly (shared drives, touchdown attribution between passer and receiver, script) and reads the probability each player has the maximum.
nfl.game_fantasy_max_field_sim.rationale: A game-most contract is not a per-player threshold: it depends on the whole field of both teams and on the strong positive correlation between a quarterback and his receivers, which makes stacking players on one offence crowd the top. ESPN scoring weights differ from Sleeper's in places, so the per-player model must be re-scored on ESPN settings before the maximum is taken.
raw_data: player-game: receptions, rushing/receiving/passing yards, touchdowns, interceptions, fumbles lost
player shares: targets, carries, red-zone opportunities

nfl.game_receiving_leader_field_sim.label: Game receiving-yards leader: joint simulation of every pass catcher in one game
nfl.game_receiving_leader_field_sim.measurement: Per game: list every WR, TE and RB with snap share >=10 percent over the last 4 games (as-of the inactive list). Draw a shared game state (plays and pass rate per team from nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior-style own ratings, no market lines), split each team's targets by Dirichlet shares centred on target share over the last 8 games (half-life 4, shrink to role prior with k=40 targets), then yards per target from nfl.player_reception_length_distribution. 20,000 simulations; P(max) with 1/N tie credit; inactive players fixed at No. Units: probability; as-of kickoff minus 90 minutes.
nfl.game_receiving_leader_field_sim.mechanism: Simulates receiving yards for all pass catchers of both teams from one shared game state so the maximum, its ties and a named player's chance of being the maximum are read jointly.
nfl.game_receiving_leader_field_sim.rationale: KXNFLMOSTRECYDS pays only if the named player beats every other catcher in the game, including the opponent's top receiver, and gives No to a non-participant. Teammates share one target pool (negative dependence) while both offences rise together in a shootout (positive dependence), so a product of marginals misprices the favourite and the long shot.
raw_data: pbp: game_id, posteam, receiver_id, complete_pass, yards_gained, air_yards

free_sources: nflverse snap counts and depth charts
nfl.game_rushing_leader_field_sim.label: Game rushing-yards leader: joint carry and yardage simulation for all ball carriers
nfl.game_rushing_leader_field_sim.measurement: Per game: rushers with carry share >=8 percent over the last 4 games plus both starting QBs. Each simulation draws a final margin from own ratings (no spread), sets team rush attempts by the score-state run-rate surface (nfl.script response with own margin), splits carries by Dirichlet shares (last 6 games, half-life 3, shrink to depth-chart role with k=30 carries) and draws per-carry yards from nfl.rush_yardage_tail. 20,000 simulations; P(max) with 1/N tie credit; inactive named player fixed at No. As-of the inactive list.
nfl.game_rushing_leader_field_sim.mechanism: Draws one game script per simulation and allocates both teams' carries among backs and quarterbacks, so the game's rushing maximum and each named runner's chance of holding it are computed jointly.
nfl.game_rushing_leader_field_sim.rationale: KXNFLMOSTRSHYDS is lost if the opposing lead back or a scrambling QB out-rushes the named player. Carries are zero-sum within a backfield and the winning side's script adds late carries to its lead back, so the leader is concentrated on the projected winner's workhorse; independent marginals overstate committee backs and understate the favourite's lead back.
raw_data: pbp: game_id, posteam, rusher_id, rush_attempt, rushing_yards, qb_scramble, score_differential

nfl.game_td_length_order_stats.label: Single-game touchdown-length order statistics (P(max >= k), P(min in band), P(no TD))
nfl.game_td_length_order_stats.measurement: For each team, N_TD ~ negative binomial with mean from nfl.model_team_td_mean (market-free) and dispersion fit on 2015+ games; per TD, route probabilities from goal-to-go share (nfl.redzone, nfl.goal_line_personnel) and non-offensive TD hazard (nfl.dst_td_hazard); length per route from the empirical 2015+ distribution of official TD distances shrunk to league with 30 TDs per team prior. Simulate 20,000 games; output bucket probabilities and P(N=0).
nfl.game_td_length_order_stats.mechanism: The longest and shortest TD of a game are the max and min of N TD lengths, N random per game and each length drawn from a route mixture (goal-line, red-zone pass, explosive scrimmage, return or recovery).
nfl.game_td_length_order_stats.rationale: Bucket markets need the whole distribution of the max and min, not a mean: the count N moves the two tails in opposite directions, zero TDs is a NO for all buckets, and integer yards with inclusive bounds create discreteness at 5/6 and 10/11 yards.

nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.label: General manager and head coach draft behavior history
nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.measurement: For each GM and head coach, compute (a) trade-down and trade-up frequency by round, (b) mean reach versus consensus rank by position in rounds 1-3, (c) positions drafted by round including late-round special-teams and positional-value habits, using their past 5 drafts with tenure weighting and shrinkage to the league mean with 3 drafts of prior weight; flag new decision makers and set a new-regime weight to the franchise's last regime at 50 percent.
nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.mechanism: Per decision-maker record of trading down, trading up for quarterbacks, positional reaches versus consensus, and tenure resets when GM or coach changes.
nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.rationale: The picks are made by a small number of people with persistent habits: some GMs trade down 40 percent of the time, others take the best available; a new GM or coach resets need and scheme (4-3 versus 3-4 edge definition). Reaches above consensus rank are a stable personal trait.

nfl.goal_line_personnel.label: Goal-line package and personnel tree (inside the 5)

nfl.goal_line_personnel.rationale: A back who plays 70% of snaps may have zero goal-line role; a 250-pound change-of-pace back may play 5% of snaps and take 60% of inside-the-3 carries. The share of snaps and the share of goal-line carries are different quantities.

nfl.goal_to_go_pass_rate.label: Team goal-to-go and inside-20 pass rate by zone and down
nfl.goal_to_go_pass_rate.measurement: From pbp 2 seasons (half-life 20 games): dropback rate in each zone by down and score_differential bucket; coach random effect shrunk with k=25 plays per zone; blend for new coordinator with league prior; output expected passing TDs fraction of team TDs given the team's red-zone trips; as-of previous game.
nfl.goal_to_go_pass_rate.mechanism: Share of snaps that are dropbacks in the zones 20-11, 10-6, 5-1 yards, by down and score state, by team and coach.
nfl.goal_to_go_pass_rate.rationale: The share of team TDs that are passing depends on goal-to-go play-calling; it varies from about 30% to 70% across teams and drives the QB's TD count more than the total.

nfl.halftime_margin_scoring_model.label: Second-half scoring by halftime margin with model-based state weights
nfl.halftime_margin_scoring_model.measurement: Condition historical Q3 and Q4 team points on halftime margin bins (<=-10, -9..-4, -3..+3, +4..+9, >=+10) and on the point-in-time model expected full-game margin from nfl.model_team_points_mean (bins |m|<3, 3-7, >7); kernel-weight by halftime margin (bandwidth 3 points) and shrink to team second-half scoring with k=15 games; pregame mixture weights over halftime states from the first-half projection of nfl.model_margin_lattice; 2009+ pbp; as-of start of week. Spreads and totals excluded, used only as benchmarks.
nfl.halftime_margin_scoring_model.mechanism: Q3 and Q4 scoring depend on the halftime margin and each team's script response; pregame 3Q, 4Q and 2H contracts are mixtures over halftime states.
nfl.halftime_margin_scoring_model.rationale: The same team scores differently leading by 14 than trailing by 3. The mixture weights must come from the model's own pregame margin so period prices are not anchored to the betting spread; second-half markets that include overtime also need the tie branch.
raw_data: pbp: score at half, qtr 3/4 scoring per team, game_seconds_remaining

nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.label: Direct-competitor leverage: remaining games among teams contending for the same slots
nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.measurement: In each weekly simulation, for each remaining game compute the change in P(contract) between simulated worlds where each team wins (leverage = |P(win)-P(loss)| x game probability uncertainty); aggregate to team-level remaining leverage by division and wild-card group; add head-to-head results to date as first-tiebreak state. Output: leverage score per game and per team.
nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.mechanism: Matrix of remaining games between teams whose division or wild-card outcomes are linked, with each game's swing in the target contract's probability.
nfl.head_to_head_leverage_games.rationale: Games among rivals are zero-sum for the division and seed contract, so they move probabilities by roughly twice as much as other games, and the head-to-head tiebreaker also locks in earlier results.

nfl.healthy_inactive_base_rate.label: Healthy-inactive and rest base rates by role and coach
nfl.healthy_inactive_base_rate.measurement: From inactive lists and injury report absences (no injury listed) 2015-2025: rate by position, age band, depth slot, team clinch status, coach; shrink to league by k=15 player-games; as-of the week.
nfl.healthy_inactive_base_rate.mechanism: Probability that a healthy player is inactive due to coach choice (rest, discipline, 46-man cut).
nfl.healthy_inactive_base_rate.rationale: About a fifth of inactives are healthy; rest decisions are concentrated in weeks 17-18 and for veterans on clinched teams.
raw_data: inactive list, injury report, snap counts

nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd.label: Conditional margin variance model
nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd.measurement: Fit quantile regression (or location-scale model with t-distributed errors) of final margin on the model mean margin and model total from nfl.model_team_points_mean (not betting lines), wind, dome, backup-QB flag and divisional flag, with data 2010+ (about 4,500 games); report conditional SD and 5/95% tail multipliers; refit annually; as-of pregame values. Betting lines are excluded from the feature set and used only to benchmark the fitted SD after the fact.
nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd.mechanism: Standard deviation and shape of the final margin as a function of expected total, spread magnitude, pace, weather and QB state.
nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd.rationale: The fixed SD of 13 points misprices tails: a low-total, windy game has a narrower margin distribution than a shootout; cover probability at +/- 10 differs by regime for the same mean.
raw_data: game results, wind, temp, roof, backup-QB flag
model mean margin and total per game (market-free)

As-of the latest game.

nfl.initial_roster_cut_model.label: Initial 53-man roster inclusion model

nfl.initial_roster_cut_model.mechanism: Probability that a player is on the initial 53-man active roster given draft round, guarantees, preseason usage, position depth and injury status.
nfl.initial_roster_cut_model.rationale: Inclusion is a constrained selection with an explicit IR/PUP exclusion; stars on IR resolve NO, while fringe players depend on dead-cap cost and roster composition.

nfl.injury_return_timeline.label: Injury-specific return-time distribution

nfl.injury_return_timeline.mechanism: Time from injury onset to first game played, by body part and severity.
nfl.injury_return_timeline.rationale: Whether a player appears in week k depends on the recovery clock; type-specific survival curves replace an undifferentiated 'injured' flag.

nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.label: Kicker ceiling range tail (make probability at 66-75 yards)
nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.measurement: Per kicker, fit a logistic make curve over distance on all regular-season attempts from 45 yards (era fixed effect from nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era), with a kicker range term from career max make, 60+ attempt history and preseason makes of 60+ yards (nfl.preseason_long_kick_evidence, down-weighted 0.5 per attempt); pre-2024 kickoff distance enters only as a prior for kickers with that history. Shrink toward the position pool with 40 attempts of prior weight; adjust for roof, altitude and wind. Output P(make | attempt at 66, 68, 70, 72 yards, neutral and favourable conditions); as-of = last game before forecast.
nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.mechanism: Per-kicker make probability beyond the demonstrated range, driven by leg speed, ball strike and launch angle, which pooled accuracy-by-distance tables cannot resolve.
nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.rationale: Existing long-kick models cover 50+ and 60+ yard attempts; a 70+ make lies beyond the regular-season record (68 yards, 2025, end of first half, indoors; previous record 66). Kickoff depth was a clean leg proxy only before the 2024 dynamic kickoff; since then (touchback to the 35 in 2025) depth is a strategic choice, so it is used only within one rule era and down-weighted, with preseason long makes as direct ceiling evidence.

nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era.label: Kicking-ball and field-goal rule era (K-ball preparation, fair-catch kick, kickoff regime)
nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era.measurement: Era indicator per season (pre-2024, 2024 dynamic kickoff, 2025+ K-ball preparation and touchback-to-35); estimate era-specific 60+ attempt rate per team-game and make rate by distance from pbp with a hierarchical prior centred on the previous era (half the era difference as prior sd); flag fair-catch free kicks separately from scrimmage FGs; as-of = league rulebook for the season.
nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era.mechanism: Rule changes alter ball flight and attempt opportunities: the 2025 rule letting kickers prepare kicking balls was followed by a jump in 60+ yard makes, and the fair-catch free kick allows an unrushed attempt scored as a field goal.
nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era.rationale: A tail fit pooled over 1999-2024 understates the current 70+ rate unless an era term is added; the post-2025 sample is small, so the era effect must be estimated with a prior and carried as uncertainty.

nfl.late_lead_clock_carry_yield.label: Late-lead clock-killing carries: expected volume and yield by back
nfl.late_lead_clock_carry_yield.measurement: Using play-by-play from the last 3 seasons, for each team compute carries per game in second-half states with lead >= 7 by back, and yards per carry in those states (shrink toward the league leading-state yield with k=25 carries). Forecast = integral over pre-game margin distribution of lead-state carries x lead-state yield, using the back depth chart at the last report. Units: carries and yards per carry.
nfl.late_lead_clock_carry_yield.mechanism: Number of carries a runner takes while his team leads in the second half and their yards per carry, which differ from neutral-game carries because defences stack boxes and runs are designed to burn clock.
nfl.late_lead_clock_carry_yield.rationale: Volume rises for favourites but each carry yields less, so counting these carries at the average yards per carry overstates yardage, and the carries often go to a different back than the one who carried in neutral situations.

nfl.late_tie_game_management.label: Late-game tie-state management policy
nfl.late_tie_game_management.measurement: From pbp: for each coach and season, rate of kneel-downs, FG attempts and go-for-it when score diff in {-3..0} and game_seconds_remaining<=120; shrink to league with k=10 occasions; compute P(tie at final | state) by state and apply to the simulated margin distribution; as-of previous week.
nfl.late_tie_game_management.mechanism: In the last two minutes with the score level, trailing by 3 or leading by 3, coaches choose between kneeling, kicking a game-winning FG, or pushing; these decisions concentrate regulation margin mass at 0.
nfl.late_tie_game_management.rationale: The margin distribution at zero is partly behavioural: a team tied with the ball inside two minutes may run the clock to guarantee overtime, and a team trailing by 3 kicks a tying FG. A smooth score model misses this.

nfl.leg_dependence_by_model_regime.label: Leg-pair dependence by model margin and total regime
nfl.leg_dependence_by_model_regime.measurement: For each leg-type pair (about 30 types), estimate Kendall tau or tetrachoric correlation of the two leg indicators within bins of the as-of pregame model expected margin from nfl.model_team_points_mean (|m|<3, 3-7, >7 points) and terciles of the model expected total, on 2015+ player-games with the model means re-computed point-in-time; shrink each bin toward the pooled estimate with k=150 games, require 400+ games per cell, report standard errors; as-of end of previous week. Closing spreads and totals are excluded and used only to benchmark.
nfl.leg_dependence_by_model_regime.mechanism: Cross-leg dependence (favourite cover with QB yards, total over with rusher yards) changes sign between competitive, blowout and shootout regimes; the regime must be assigned from the model's own pregame expectation.
nfl.leg_dependence_by_model_regime.rationale: One correlation coefficient averages positive shootout dependence with negative blowout dependence. Assigning regimes by the betting spread would make the combo price depend on the market line; using the model margin keeps the input market-free and lets the model disagree with the line.
raw_data: player-game stats: passing_yards, rushing_yards, receptions, tds

nfl.long_fg_attempt_and_make_model.rationale: The 60+ yard season contract needs the number of attempts (a coaching and game-state decision, usually at the end of halves) and a steeply falling make probability, both with strong venue and kicker dependence.

nfl.model_margin_lattice.label: Model-based regulation margin lattice with mass at zero (key-number corrected, end-of-game behaviour included)
nfl.model_margin_lattice.measurement: Simulate 20,000 games per matchup from per-drive outcome multinomials (TD with 94 percent extra-point conversion, FG, safety, no score) calibrated so team means equal the market-free model team means, then fit an isotonic correction of simulated P(margin=k) to empirical regulation-margin frequencies (all regular-season games since 2002, about 5,500, binned by model |mean margin| in 0-3, 3-6, 6-10, 10+ points and model total terciles) with Beta(a=2, b=30) shrinkage in each bin for k=0 and Dirichlet smoothing for key numbers 3, 6, 7, 10, 14. Add an end-of-game term for tied games where the team with the ball inside two minutes can run the clock. Output P(margin=k) for k from -30 to 30. As-of: latest model means at kickoff minus 90 minutes; no spread, total or price enters.
nfl.model_margin_lattice.mechanism: Probability that the regulation margin equals k, especially k=0, from a drive-outcome simulation or lattice centred on the market-free team means, corrected for the excess mass that 3-point and 7-point scoring and late tie-forcing behaviour put on small margins.
nfl.model_margin_lattice.rationale: Tie, overtime and integer-spread markets are priced on atoms at specific margins, which a smooth normal density misses; a lattice centred on betting-line residuals would import the market's own view of the game. Centring on the model mean margin and total from the market-free team means keeps the input market-free and lets the line serve as a benchmark only.

nfl.model_team_points_mean.label: Market-free team expected points and margin (drive-model mean and SD per team)
nfl.model_team_points_mean.measurement: For team i vs opponent j, expected points = E[drives_i] x E[points per drive_i]. E[drives] = 3600 / (mean seconds per drive implied by both teams' neutral-situation seconds per play and expected plays per drive), 2015+ regular-season pbp, ridge-shrunk 50/50 toward league mean at 8 games. Points per drive from a ridge regression on own opponent-adjusted offensive EPA per play (exponential half-life 8 games, prior-season carryover weight 0.3 decaying to 0 by week 10), opponent defensive EPA per play, red-zone TD rate (shrunk k=30 trips), kicker FG-range rating, starting-QB indicator, wind above 15 mph and dome flags, home indicator. Output team mean, SD (from residuals by tercile) and the margin and total means as differences and sums. As-of timestamp: after the previous game and re-run at the latest injury report. Betting lines are excluded from the feature set and used only for after-the-fact benchmarking.
nfl.model_team_points_mean.mechanism: Each team's expected points are expected drives times points per drive, built from opponent-adjusted offence and defence efficiency, tempo, kicker and quarterback status and weather, with no betting line, price or implied total used as a feature.
nfl.model_team_points_mean.rationale: Market-derived team means (spread and total splits) are benchmarks that already contain the market's injury, weather and sharp information; feeding them into a model of the same game makes the model unable to show any independent information and hides which fundamental channels are missing. A market-free mean keeps the availability, weather, matchup and coaching channels explicit and lets the line be used only as an evaluation benchmark.

nfl.model_team_td_mean.label: Market-free team touchdown mean (drives times TD-per-drive, with FG-vs-TD split)
nfl.model_team_td_mean.measurement: lambda_TD(team i vs j) = E[drives_i] x P(TD | drive). E[drives] from both teams' neutral seconds per play and expected plays (2015+ pbp, shrink 50/50 to league at 8 games). P(TD|drive) = logistic ridge on own opponent-adjusted offensive EPA per play (half-life 8 games, prior-season weight 0.3 fading to 0 by week 10), opponent defensive EPA per play, red-zone trips per drive and red-zone TD rate (shrunk k=30 trips), 4th-and-goal go-for-it rate (k=12), wind>15 mph and dome flags, starting-QB indicator. Output mean, variance (overdispersion from tercile residuals) and P(N>=1)=1-exp(-lambda_TD) with a negative-binomial correction. As-of: after the previous game, refreshed at the final injury report. Spreads, totals and prices excluded; used only afterwards as a benchmark.
nfl.model_team_td_mean.mechanism: A team's expected touchdowns are expected drives times the per-drive probability of ending in a touchdown rather than a field goal or no score, estimated from opponent-adjusted offence and defence and red-zone conversion, with no spread, total or price as a feature.
nfl.model_team_td_mean.rationale: Every scorer market is a share of the team's touchdown pool. A points-based implied team total is market-derived and is not touchdown-specific (24 points can be 3 TD + FG or 2 TD + 3 FG). A model-derived TD mean keeps wind, availability and matchup visible and gives P(team scores at least one TD), the quantity the team-own first-TD contract depends on.
