nfl.multi_season_playoff_drought_hazard.label: Multi-season playoff-appearance hazard (season of next playoff appearance)
nfl.multi_season_playoff_drought_hazard.measurement: Year-end own rating (nfl.own_team_rating_market_free) evolves as r_{t+1} = 0.67 r_t + e, e ~ N(0, sd fitted on 2002-2025 year-to-year changes, about 4.5 points), with an added jump term when the starting QB changes (probability from contract year, age and draft capital; size from nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop). P(playoffs | rating) per season from the standings simulation calibrated on 14-team formats (2020+). Simulate 20,000 paths of 6 seasons; P(first appearance in season s); apply the franchise-continuity clause as a negligible hazard. As-of the latest game.
nfl.multi_season_playoff_drought_hazard.mechanism: The season in which a team next makes the playoffs is a first-passage time of a mean-reverting team-strength process over several seasons, with jumps from quarterback and coaching changes.
nfl.multi_season_playoff_drought_hazard.rationale: KXNFLENDSTREAK pays on the specific future season of the next playoff appearance; this year's standings simulation answers only the current season, while later seasons depend on how fast NFL ratings revert (roughly one third per year), draft capital from bad seasons and the chance of a new starting quarterback, which a one-season model cannot give.
raw_data: starting QB by team-season and QB change flags

nfl.multi_td_dispersion.label: Within-player multi-TD dispersion factor
nfl.multi_td_dispersion.measurement: Fit a negative-binomial dispersion r by position group (RB goal-line, WR1, TE, QB rush) on the last 5 seasons of player-games with at least 4 expected TD-opportunity touches; report r and P(2+|P(1+)) lookup table; as-of start of week.
nfl.multi_td_dispersion.mechanism: A player's TDs share a latent intensity (team total and goal-line role), so P(2+) exceeds the Poisson implied by P(1+).
nfl.multi_td_dispersion.rationale: 2+ TD contracts and 'multiple touchdowns' markets are priced off the same marginal intensity; dispersion decides the tail ratio P(2+)/P(1+).
raw_data: player-game TD counts, xTD by game

free_sources: nflverse play-by-play (touchdown with td_team differing from posteam, safety flag)
nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.label: Non-offensive scoring rate: defensive and special-teams points for and against
nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.measurement: Per team, count of defensive and special-teams scoring plays per game over the last 25 games with half-life 12, shrunk heavily toward league (k=40 games) because these events are rare; split into takeaway-driven part (own takeaway rate x return-score probability) and special-teams part; opponent's rate against the team computed symmetrically. Output expected points and probability of at least one such score.
nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.mechanism: Expected points per game from interception returns, fumble returns, kick and punt return touchdowns and safeties credited to the team, and the equivalent against it.
nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.rationale: These points enter the team's total independent of offence, and when scored against the team they end drives; ignoring them biases rungs low for teams with opportunistic defences.
raw_data: pbp: td_team, posteam, interception, fumble_lost, return_touchdown, safety

free_sources: league transactions page and Pro-Football-Reference transactions (free_scrape)
nfl.non_roster_return_status.label: Non-roster status transition model (retired, free agent, suspended or unsigned player returning to play)
nfl.non_roster_return_status.measurement: P(plays in week w) = P(contract signed by the week-w roster deadline) x P(activated and takes a snap | signed). Estimate the first factor as a discrete-time hazard on retired and unsigned veterans 2000-2025 (age, years since last game, Pro Bowl count, stated intent in the previous 12 months as a binary flag, team contract interest reported by named insiders as a binary flag with a timestamp, days to the target week), with ridge shrinkage and a Beta(1, 19) prior for the base comeback rate; estimate the second from signing-to-first-snap lags of mid-season veteran signings (median lag in weeks, shrunk with k=8 signings). For NEXTTEAM contracts output P(team k) by multinomial logit on prior-team cap space, position need and reported interest, with a 'retires or no team' category. As-of: each transaction-wire timestamp and insider report time.
nfl.non_roster_return_status.mechanism: A player who is not on an active roster can only take a snap after a chain of discrete events: ending retirement or suspension, signing with a team, passing a physical, and being activated, each with its own timing and decision-maker.
nfl.non_roster_return_status.rationale: The injury-report-to-inactive-list mechanism does not apply to a retired or unsigned player such as the sampled KXNFLWEEKCOMPETE subject (a player outside any current roster); the live contracts KXNFLRETURN and KXNFLNEXTTEAM are also status-transition events, so a separate model with reference classes for comebacks is required.
raw_data: transaction wire: player, event type, date, team
player status history: retired flag, last game date, age

nfl.ol_individual_protection_record.label: Offensive-lineman protection record: pressures and sacks allowed per pass-block snap
nfl.ol_individual_protection_record.measurement: Per lineman-season to date: pressures allowed and sacks allowed per 100 pass-block snaps (PFF or SIS charting), penalties per 100 snaps, starts, and team sack rate adjusted for QB time to throw; shrink each rate toward position mean with k=300 pass-block snaps; composite z-score plus prior-honour indicator (All-Pro or Pro Bowl in last 2 seasons). As-of each week; final as-of end of regular season.
nfl.ol_individual_protection_record.mechanism: Measures an offensive lineman's pass protection (pressures and sacks allowed per pass-block snap, penalties), games started and team context, the evidence a Protector of the Year vote would reward.
nfl.ol_individual_protection_record.rationale: Linemen have no counting statistics in box scores, so voters lean on charting grades, reputation (prior All-Pro/Pro Bowl) and team sack rate; the individual pressure-allowed rate is paid charting data and team sack rate confounds the quarterback's habits, which is the subtle part.
raw_data: lineman pass-block snaps, pressures and sacks allowed (charting)
team sack rate and QB time to throw
prior All-Pro and Pro Bowl selections

nfl.opening_kick_field_position.label: Opening kickoff field position distribution by returner and rule regime
nfl.opening_kick_field_position.measurement: Per team's returner and kicker: P(touchback), mean starting yardline_100 after kick, return TD per kickoff, shrunk to league by season with k=20 kicks; flag the season-specific rule; as-of week.
nfl.opening_kick_field_position.mechanism: Starting yard line after the opening kickoff (touchback spot, return average, return TD risk).
nfl.opening_kick_field_position.rationale: Field position at drive 1 changes TD probability for the first drive; rule changes alter the touchback spot and return frequency season to season.
raw_data: pbp: kickoff_attempt, touchback, kick_returner_player_id, yardline_100 after kick

nfl.opp_def_int_propensity.label: Opponent defence interception propensity, QB-quality adjusted
nfl.opp_def_int_propensity.measurement: Interceptions per attempt faced by the defence, adjusted by opposing QB turnover-worthy rate (season), pressure rate faced and pass depth; regress to league mean with k=350 attempts; recency half-life 12 games; as-of previous game.
nfl.opp_def_int_propensity.mechanism: Opponent's interceptions per attempt over expectation given the quality of QBs faced and pressure generated.
nfl.opp_def_int_propensity.rationale: Interception counts by defence are heavily luck; the skill component (ball skills, safety range) must be separated from the pressure effect and from opposing QB quality.

nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.label: Opponent ball-control denial: expected drives and time removed from this offence
nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.measurement: For each opponent compute average seconds per play, run rate in neutral situations and drive length over the last 12 games (half-life 6); expected own drives = league drives x (own-share model) where own share = own pace / (own pace + opponent pace) adjusted by a regression on historical game drive counts; output expected drives for each side and variance. As-of last game.
nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.mechanism: How much the opponent's time of possession, run share and clock usage cut this offence's number of drives relative to its neutral pace.
nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial.rationale: A team's own tempo says nothing about drives if the opponent holds the ball; the effect depends on the matchup of styles and is not captured by pace alone.
raw_data: pbp: drive, posteam, game_seconds_remaining, play_clock info

nfl.ot_ending_hazard.label: P(game ends level | overtime) under current OT rules
nfl.ot_ending_hazard.measurement: Simulate OT as a drive process with period length 10 min (regular season), possession rule per season, team TD/FG rates per drive (from nfl.drive-level data, shrunk), and 4th-down aggression; calibrate to realized OT outcomes since 2012 (about 100+ regular-season OT games); report P(level | OT) with credible interval; as-of start of season and refreshed weekly.
nfl.ot_ending_hazard.mechanism: Probability that the overtime period fails to produce a decisive score, given each team's possession counts, scoring rates and 4th-down choices under the OT rule set.
nfl.ot_ending_hazard.rationale: Overtime ending level is a very small but rule-dependent event; the tie market is the product of two small probabilities and the OT-rule change makes historical frequencies stale.

nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.label: Own-one-yard-line snap rate (offence backed up at its own 1)
nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.measurement: Per team-game, count snaps with yardline_100 = 99 (offence at own 1) from nflverse play-by-play, excluding kneels. Fit a negative-binomial rate on opponent-adjusted punting (inside-10 rate, net punt), defence goal-line stand rate and team penalty profile with 3-season pooling and shrinkage toward the league mean (about 30 team-games of prior weight). Output expected count for each remaining game; as-of = last completed game before the forecast.
nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.mechanism: An offensive scrimmage gain can be at most 99 yards and only from a snap at the offence's own 1-yard line, so the count of such snaps is the exposure for the offensive route to a 99+ yard play.
nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.rationale: Snaps from the 1 are produced by punts downed or fumbled at the 1, goal-line stands that end in a turnover on downs, and penalties walking the ball back; they are rare, clustered in a few team-games and not stable team traits. The contract is therefore a Poisson-thinning problem whose rate is this count, not any player's long-run yardage.
